verdict: Uber grew revenue 20% to $13.5B on 22% more trips, but operating profit rose only 5% to $1.1B as legal reserves swelled — the headline $6.6B net income came mostly from a $4.9B one-off tax benefit and $1.5B of investment gains.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 20% to $25.1B.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers. Gross Bookings rose 25% to $23.3B.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue and bookings were flat.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Running the platform day to day — support, operations and local teams.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Promotions, advertising and winning riders, eaters and drivers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its autonomous-vehicle partnerships.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and the back office. This quarter it absorbed $479M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes and settlements.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of equipment and past acquisitions over their useful lives.

follow100Note: Of the $49.40 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $0.19 belongs to non-controlling partners — $49.21 is Uber shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trips still booming
takeaways.text: Trips grew 22% to 3.5 billion and Gross Bookings 21% to $49.7B, with Monthly Active Platform Consumers up 17%. Revenue grew 20% to $13.5B — Mobility +20%, Delivery +29%, Freight flat.

takeaways.title: Legal reserves hit operating profit
takeaways.text: Income from operations rose just 5% to $1.1B: general & administrative costs jumped to $1,183M as Uber booked $479M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes and settlements. Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes them, rose 33% to $2.3B.

takeaways.title: A tax release made the bottom line
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Uber was $6.6B ($3.11 a share) — but $4.9B of it was a non-cash benefit from releasing a tax valuation allowance, and other income included a $1.5B net gain on revaluations of Uber's equity investments.

oneTimers: A $4.9B non-cash tax benefit from releasing valuation allowances against deferred tax assets sits in the tax line (a $4,046M net tax benefit for the quarter) — it reflects Uber's sustained profitability, not cash received.
Other income includes a $1.5B net benefit (pre-tax) from revaluations of Uber's equity investments — paper gains on stakes it holds.
General & administrative expense includes $479M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes and settlements, which Uber excludes from Adjusted EBITDA.
otherDetail: Other income, net of $1,619M — mostly a $1.5B net gain on revaluations of Uber's equity investments, plus interest income — less $112M of interest expense and a $14M equity-method loss.
footerNote: Net income of $6,652M includes $26M attributable to non-controlling interests; $6,626M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $3.11 EPS figure).
